nodes.description: INF2 is strongly expressed in Schwann-cell cytoplasm, where it colocalises and interacts with myelin and lymphocyte protein (MAL) and engages the Rho-family GTPase CDC42 - both of them proteins implicated in myelination and myelin maintenance. evidence.reference_title: Neuropathologic characterization of INF2-related Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease: evidence for a Schwann cell actinopathy.
evidence.snippet: Pathologic lesions suggested chronic demyelination and remyelination associated with progressive axonal loss.

nodes.description: Kidney disease can progress to end-stage renal disease in adolescence. Seven of eight patients in the Japanese neuropathy cohort reached this endpoint at a median age of 15 years. This selected clinical series does not establish lifetime risk for all INF2 neuropathy carriers.

evidence.reference_title: INF2-Related Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease in a Japanese Cohort: Genetic and Clinical Insights.
evidence.snippet: All patients also developed kidney dysfunction, with 7/8 (88%) progressing to end-stage renal disease at a median age of 15 years.

nodes.description: R218Q expression in renal epithelial cells promotes nuclear accumulation of MRTF and sustained MRTF-SRF transcriptional activity. This is an experimental renal-allele mechanism whose relevance to CMT-associated kidney disease is indirect.

evidence.reference_title: INF2 formin variants linked to human inherited kidney disease reprogram the transcriptome, causing mitotic chaos and cell death.
evidence.snippet: In line with the effect of INF2 R218Q on MRTF nuclear translocation, INF2 R218Q caused a considerable increase of MRTF-SRF transcriptional activity, an effect that was reduced by LatB

nodes.description: Vincristine can markedly worsen hereditary neuropathy; treatment planning should consider this risk with the oncology and neurology teams.
